front_end_yields.note: Two-year up 6bp to 4.72, highest since July 2024.

long_end_yields.note: 30-year fell ~2bp; chair cited growth, capital competition, geopolitics.

yield_curve.note: Front end up, long end down; curve flattened after hawkish Fed.

dollar.note: Dollar ascendant; DXY move cited at 2.8 standard deviations.

oil.note: Crude up over 20% since last Fed meeting; oil driving inflation.

credit_spreads.note: Credit spreads described as down despite heavy supply.

equity_futures.note: S&P fell after hawkish Fed; banks hammered.

fed.market_pricing: >90% odds of 25bp hike; front end priced multiple hikes.

earnings_ai.note: Earnings strong and AI capex robust, but AI adds inflation and capital competition.

geopolitics.note: Middle East war and oil shock cited; geopolitical uncertainty increased.

consumer.note: Retail sales strong, but high fuel prices and price tolerance concerns.

key_catalysts: Middle East conflict and oil shock
brief.summary: The Fed delivered a unanimous 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% and signaled another increase this year, with a hawkish Warsh press conference. Front-end yields rose and the curve flattened, while long-end yields slipped; the dollar strengthened and oil stayed sharply higher. Equities turned lower and banks sold off as markets priced more tightening. The dominant narrative is a Fed that has lost patience with above-target inflation despite strong growth and earnings, while oil and geopolitics add supply shocks. The show's tone was risk-off and hawkish, though the US economy was repeatedly described as resilient.
notable_quotes: Today's policy action will support a timely return to the committee's two percent goal.
I would be hard pressed to describe financial conditions as restrictive.
